task.description: WF-01 Step 2 HARD GATE: independently validate REQ-219 (supervision-tree layering, closes ISS-0425 parts 1+partial-2) and REQ-220 (Task.Supervisor sprawl review, closes ISS-0425 part 3), drafted by REQ-ANALYST. Ran all five WF-01 Step 2 checks (testability, consistency, depends_on, stage fit, sizing) against each, plus REQ-219-specific checks on AC4's crash-loop testability, independent verification of the real 20-child list in lib/letflow/application.ex against REQ-219's stated layer assignment, independent verification of both hand-maintained ordering constraints (ISS-0224, ISS-0429), independent re-derivation of the :one_for_one-over-:rest_for_one justification against real name-based lookup usage in the codebase, and independent verification of REQ-220's 'all 7 Task.Supervisors have a real, distinct reason' claim against application.ex's actual inline comments.
acceptance_criteria: Every check actually run against both requirements by reading the requirement text and the real application.ex, not assumed from REQ-ANALYST's summary.
All 20 children in application.ex's real child list independently enumerated and cross-checked against REQ-219's layer-membership text.

Both ISS-0224 and ISS-0429 ordering constraints checked for whether REQ-219's acceptance criteria make preservation an explicit, checkable/testable requirement, not merely an assumption embedded in prose.
The :rest_for_one rejection re-derived independently by grepping for pid-based vs. name-based Task.Supervisor/process lookups in lib/letflow/, not trusted from the requirement's own claim.
REQ-220's per-Task.Supervisor justification claims checked against application.ex's real inline comments, one by one.

result.summary: REQ-220 passes every check cleanly. REQ-219 FAILS check #3 (ordering-constraint preservation is not actually made a checkable/testable requirement for ISS-0429, only for ISS-0224) -- a concrete, actionable gap, not a stylistic nitpick. Both requirements are otherwise well-constructed; only REQ-219 needs rework before either is eligible for WF-02 registration (REQ-220 depends_on REQ-219 and cannot register independently of it).

req219.1_testability: PASS. AC4 (crash-loop reproduction, Repo pid unaffected) is genuinely testable, not just aspirational: application.ex's own existing comments (lines 158-164, scheduler_children/0) document that this exact DBConnection.OwnershipError crash-loop was 'verified live via a full mix test run' historically, before the :start_scheduler gate was added -- i.e. the mechanism AC4 asks to be reproduced is not hypothetical, it is the documented real incident that motivated the current test-mode gate. A test can reproduce it deterministically by starting Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers with :start_scheduler true under Ecto sandbox :manual mode without allowing the connection, which will force the real Poller to raise on every zero-delay tick; because Pollers' max_restarts:5/max_seconds:60 tolerates only 5 restarts and the ticks are effectively immediate, the 60-second window is generous rather than restrictive -- the test will complete in well under a second, not require an actual 60s wait. Capturing Repo's pid via Process.whereis/1 before and after is straightforward ExUnit. Other ACs (AC1, AC2's grep/structural proof, AC6's config-file-unchanged claim) are all concretely falsifiable.
req219.2_layer_assignment_completeness: PASS, independently verified against the real lib/letflow/application.ex (read in full, 2026-09-03). The real child list has exactly 20 entries in this order: Letflow.Repo, Ecto.Migrator, Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker, Letflow.Registry, Letflow.Metrics.Registry, Letflow.Admission, Letflow.InstanceSupervisor, SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor, Letflow.SandboxPool, Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor, Engine.PluginRegistry, Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry, Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor, Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor, Letflow.Scheduler.Poller (gated), Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller (gated), Bandit (gated). REQ-219's decision 2 layer-membership list assigns exactly these 17 to Infrastructure (in the same relative order), 2 to Pollers, 1 to Http = 20/20, no child missed or duplicated, no misclassification found.
req219.3_ordering_constraint_preservation: FAIL -- this is the blocking finding. ISS-0224's constraint (SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor before SandboxPool) IS made an explicit, checkable requirement: AC2 states 'ISS-0224's SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor-before-SandboxPool ordering still holds (explicit test or documented startup-order proof)', a concrete, gate-able bar. ISS-0429's constraint (Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor reachable before either Poller's first zero-delay tick) is NOT made checkable the same way. Decision 4(b)'s argument -- 'Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure completes its ENTIRE startup ... before Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers starts at all' -- is architecturally sound (Supervisor.start_link/2 starts children sequentially, each child's own init/1 and subtree fully up before the next starts), BUT that guarantee only holds if Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure is actually listed BEFORE Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers in Letflow.Application's own top-level children list. Neither decision 1 ('three new sibling supervisor modules ... become the ONLY 3 children ... under strategy: :one_for_one', no order stated) nor AC1 (line 13076: 'takes exactly 3 children -- Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure, Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, Letflow.Supervisor.Http ... under strategy: :one_for_one; none of the 20 current leaf children ... remain directly in Letflow.Application's own children list -- confirmed by reading application.ex') actually requires this specific list ORDER. AC1 names the three modules but never states they must appear in that order in the actual list -- an implementation that lists them as [Pollers, Infrastructure, Http] (or any other order) would satisfy every word of AC1 as written while silently breaking decision 4(b)'s entire ISS-0429 argument, since Pollers' first zero-delay tick could then reach Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor before Infrastructure has even started. The only place this ordering constraint is checked at all is AC8's REVIEWER sign-off ('the new 3-layer shape does not weaken ISS-0224's or ISS-0429's real ordering guarantee') -- a review judgment, not a grep-verifiable or test-verifiable acceptance criterion, unlike every other structural claim in this requirement's own AC list (AC1's 'confirmed by reading application.ex', AC2's 'explicit test or documented startup-order proof', AC4's induced-crash-loop test, AC6's 'confirmed by mix test passing'). This is a real asymmetry within the requirement's own text, not a hypothetical: the requirement explicitly set out to make ISS-0429's ordering 'now structural' (line 13046) but never actually pins down the one list-order fact that structural guarantee depends on, as its own checkable AC.
req219.4_rest_for_one_rejection: PASS, independently re-derived. Grepped lib/letflow/ for every live Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/async_nolink/start_child call site (sandbox_pool.ex:604, plugin_interface.ex:187, module_registry.ex:258, capability_gate.ex:452, module_version_registry.ex:306/392/486, lua/executor.ex:367, obs/alerts.ex:449) -- every single one dispatches against a compile-time module-name atom (e.g. Letflow.Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor, @task_supervisor module attribute set to a name), never a stored pid captured from a prior lookup. The same holds for Letflow.Repo (named Ecto repo, looked up by module name) and the Registries. This confirms REQ-219's own claim that no Infrastructure child is depended on by stored pid anywhere in Poller or Http code -- the entire dependency graph is name-based lookup, which is exactly the precondition decision 1's :one_for_one-over-:rest_for_one argument requires. The rejection of ISS-0425's own 'candidate shape' (:rest_for_one) is well-reasoned and independently verified, not merely asserted.
req219.5_depends_on: N/A for REQ-219 itself (depends_on: [REQ-214, REQ-216], both correct REQ-id references, both real prerequisites -- REQ-214 added the second Poller this requirement re-homes, REQ-216 added Letflow.Admission, one of the 20 children being layered). PASS.
req219.6_sizing: PASS, with a note (non-blocking). ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis suggested a 3-way split (core layering, apply-to-both-Pollers, Task.Supervisor review); REQ-ANALYST merged the first two into REQ-219. This is justified, not scope inflation: 'apply the settled layer shape to both Pollers' is not a separable deliverable from 'decide the layer shape' here, because the two existing Pollers are exactly the children whose current flat-peer placement is the documented incident this requirement exists to fix -- landing the layer shape without moving both Pollers into it would leave the requirement's own AC4 crash-loop fix undone. A restructuring of application.ex cannot be safely half-done (an intermediate state with only some children moved risks breaking startup entirely, per ISSUE-FIXER's own blast-radius point). REQ-220 correctly stays split out, since it is a genuinely separable, lower-stakes documentation pass that only needs REQ-219's Infrastructure module to exist as a home for its consolidated comment.
req219.7_iss0421_iss0422_exclusion: PASS. REQ-219's 'NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT' section correctly names and excludes ISS-0421's own scope ('ISS-0421's own internal Poller fix... separate, narrower, sequenced to land after this requirement') and ISS-0422's own scope ('ISS-0422's CLAUDE.md/requirements.yaml wording drift -- confirmed documentation-only and unrelated'), matching both issues' real, current scope as read in docs/issues/ISS-0421.yaml and ISS-0422.yaml via ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis. No accidental absorption or contradiction found.

req220.1_testability: PASS. AC1-AC4 are concrete: a single consolidated list with per-supervisor justification and originating REQ/ISS id, an explicit consider-and-reject pass on the two most plausible consolidation candidates (three Wasm supervisors; Plugin+Lua), a no-side-effect-merge constraint gated by REVIEWER sign-off if a deviation is ever proposed, and mix test/compile passing.
req220.2_consistency: PASS. Explicitly builds on REQ-219's Infrastructure module and does not re-open REQ-219's layer assignment; NOT-IN-THIS-REQUIREMENT section is clean.
req220.3_depends_on: PASS. depends_on: [REQ-219] -- confirmed against this file's real, consistently-used convention (REQ-ids only, never queue_task_id/impl_order: cross-checked REQ-214's depends_on: [REQ-056, REQ-204], REQ-215's depends_on: [REQ-214, REQ-177, REQ-049, REQ-061], REQ-217/218's depends_on: [REQ-216] -- all REQ-id-only). REQ-220 correctly depends on REQ-219 alone (the requirement's own stated reason -- avoiding two requirements editing the same application.ex section concurrently -- is accurate and sufficient).
req220.4_stage_fit: PASS. S6, same stage as REQ-219 and the rest of the current admission-control/scheduler/observability work.
req220.5_sizing: PASS. A single documentation-consolidation pass over one file's existing comments plus a bounded compile/test check; correctly small relative to REQ-219.
req220.8_all_7_justifications_verified: PASS, independently re-read against lib/letflow/application.ex's real inline comments (2026-09-03): SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor (ISS-0224, lines 67-71, claim/2 async_nolink isolation) -- matches. Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor (REQ-057, line 74, generic plugin-handler execution) -- matches (no inline comment on this exact line but plugin_interface.ex:171 confirms). Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor (REQ-155, lines 76-80, wall-clock kill isolation, deliberately not sharing PluginTaskSupervisor) -- matches verbatim. Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor (REQ-166, lines 82-92, unresolved-import EXIT isolation, upload-time-only, deliberately not reused) -- matches verbatim. Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor (REQ-167, lines 94-102, same crash-isolation need but orthogonal caller/input per req166 §2.2, deliberately not reusing ModuleRegistry's) -- matches verbatim. Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor (REQ-173, lines 104-113, hot-reload invoke/4's outer task plus nested instantiation task) -- matches verbatim. Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor (ISS-0429, lines 114-133, I/O-bound HTTP alert-hook delivery, independent of sandbox/plugin/Lua/Wasm) -- matches verbatim, including the load-bearing ordering comment. Every one of REQ-220's 7 stated justifications is an accurate restatement of the real, currently-on-record reason, not an invented or stretched one.

issues.description: REQ-219 (docs/requirements.yaml, requirement starting line 12949) makes ISS-0429's ordering constraint 'structural' in prose (decision 4(b), around line 13046: 'Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure completes its ENTIRE startup ... before Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers starts at all') but never states, as an actual acceptance criterion, the one fact that structural guarantee depends on: that Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure must appear BEFORE Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers in Letflow.Application's own top-level children list passed to Supervisor.start_link/2. AC1 (line 13076) names the three required children but not their required relative order; AC8's REVIEWER sign-off is a review judgment, not a grep- or test-verifiable criterion, and no other AC covers it. Contrast with ISS-0224's constraint, which AC2 makes explicitly checkable ('explicit test or documented startup-order proof'). As written, an implementation could satisfy every literal word of REQ-219's AC list while listing the three sub-supervisors in an order that reintroduces exactly the crash window ISS-0429 fixed.
issues.fix_required: Add an explicit, checkable acceptance criterion to REQ-219 requiring that Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure appears before Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers in Letflow.Application's own top-level children list (grep-verifiable, e.g. 'Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure's list index precedes Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers' list index in Letflow.Application.start/2's children list -- grep/read-verified'), and ideally add or extend AC4's crash-loop test (or a lighter dedicated test) to assert Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor is already registered (Process.whereis/1 non-nil) at the moment Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers begins running, giving ISS-0429's guarantee the same test-backed bar ISS-0224's already has via AC2, not review judgment alone.

result.next_action: Rework REQ-ANALYST -- 1 BLOCKER above on REQ-219 (add an explicit, checkable top-level-list-order acceptance criterion + strengthen the ISS-0429 ordering test bar to match ISS-0224's). REQ-220 needs no changes and can be re-submitted unchanged once REQ-219 is fixed; re-validate both together in the same follow-up pass since REQ-220's depends_on: [REQ-219] means it cannot register for WF-02 independently.
